mainTopic: The צרה of an ערוה: the end of the משנה, the sources for בית שמאי, and whether differing practices break לא תתגודדו
overview: The משנה finishes the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about the צרה of an ערוה. It explains what happens to her fitness for כהונה after חליצה or יבום. It adds that the two schools still married into each other's families and relied on each other in טהרות. The גמרא gives רבי שמעון בן פזי's source for בית שמאי from the word ״החוצה״, and the two schools trade readings of ״חוצה״, ״לאיש זר״ and the extra ה. רבא then offers a different reason for בית שמאי: אין איסור חל על איסור, which works whichever brother married first. The גמרא explains why the משנה needed its lines about חליצה and יבום, pointing to רבי יוחנן בן נורי's proposal. Finally, ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether different מגילה reading days break לא תתגודדו, 'do not form separate groups'. Their back-and-forth about ערב פסח leads to the visible dispute over the צרות, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Results of חליצה or יבום for the co-wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what happens to the co-wife's fitness to marry a כהן if she did חליצה or יבום, according to each school.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the co-wives did חליצה, בית שמאי say they may no longer marry a כהן, and בית הלל say they still may. If they did יבום, בית שמאי say they may still marry a כהן, and בית הלל say they may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing the מחלוקת about the צרה of an ערוה by showing what follows in practice from each side's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי the צרה really needs יבום, so her חליצה is a real חליצה, and a חלוצה may not marry a כהן. For בית הלל she was never bound to the brother at all, so the חליצה means nothing and she stays fit. The same logic reverses for יבום: for בית הלל it was a forbidden relationship, so she becomes unfit for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: They did חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
They were taken in יבום, married by the brother-in-law
They make her unfit to marry a כהן
They declare her fit

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the flip. בית שמאי are stricter after חליצה but more lenient after יבום, and בית הלל are the opposite. Each side is just following its own basic view of whether the צרה was bound to the brother.

phrases.aramaic: חָלְצוּ — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין מִן הַכְּהוּנָּה,
phrases.english: If they performed חליצה, Beit Shammai disqualify them from the priesthood,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the co-wives of the forbidden relative, the case the משנה was just talking about.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel deem them fit.
If they were taken in levirate marriage, Beit Shammai deem them fit,
and Beit Hillel disqualify them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלְצוּ — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי פּוֹסְלִין מִן הַכְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's מחלוקת about the צרות from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After חליצה: בית שמאי disqualify from כהונה and בית הלל allow. After יבום: בית שמאי allow and בית הלל disqualify.

steps.title: The two schools still married each other and shared purity
steps.stepSummary: Despite their disputes, בית שמאי and בית הלל kept marrying into each other's families and handling pure items together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though one side forbids and the other permits, and one side disqualifies and the other declares fit, בית שמאי did not hold back from marrying women from בית הלל, and בית הלל did not hold back from marrying women from בית שמאי. The same goes for all their disputes about טהרה and טומאה: they still prepared pure items relying on each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a closing remark about how the two schools lived together in spite of serious halachic disagreements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might expect that people who think the other side's marriages are forbidden would refuse to marry them. The משנה reports that they did not refuse. It reports the same about טהרות: each side still relied on the other in matters of purity.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbid and permit
They did not hold back or refrain
Matters of ritual purity and impurity
Each with the other, relying on one another

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה closes by stressing that serious halachic disagreement did not stop בית שמאי and בית הלל from marrying into each other's families or relying on each other in טהרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line raises an obvious question: how could they marry each other if one side considers some of those marriages forbidden? That question is a natural point for further discussion.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵלּוּ אוֹסְרִים וְאֵלּוּ מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: Although these prohibit and those permit,
these disqualify and those deem fit,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְנְעוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מִלִּישָּׂא נָשִׁים מִבֵּית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai did not refrain from marrying women from Beit Hillel,
nor did Beit Hillel refrain from marrying women from Beit Shammai.
All the matters of purity and impurity
where these would rule pure and those would rule impure,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְנְעוּ עוֹשִׂין טְהָרוֹת אֵלּוּ עַל גַּבֵּי אֵלּוּ.
phrases.english: they did not refrain from preparing pure items with each other.
phrases.notes: Literally 'these on top of these.' He means they used each other's vessels and trusted each other about purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵלּוּ אוֹסְרִים וְאֵלּוּ מַתִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical, social comment on the disputes just listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Despite their disputes, the two schools married into each other's families and relied on each other in טהרות.

steps.title: The source for בית שמאי's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן פזי derives from the word 'החוצה' that even when one wife is 'inside' the family, the 'outside' co-wife still needs יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said: What is the reason of בית שמאי? The פסוק says, 'The wife of the dead man shall not be outside, to a stranger.' The word 'outside' implies that there is also an 'inside' wife. Even so, the תורה says the outside one 'shall not be' married to a stranger, so she must go to יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the Torah source of בית שמאי, who say the co-wife of an ערוה must do יבום, and it answers from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'החוצה' ('the outside one') hints that there is also a wife who is 'inside.' That inside wife is the one closely related to the יבם, the ערוה. The פסוק still commands that the 'outside' co-wife not marry a stranger, which means she remains bound to the brother for יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What is the reason?
The one outside, the wife who is outside the family
This implies there is an inside one
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said:
What is the reason of Beit Shammai?
As it is written: 'The wife of the dead man shall not be'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

phrases.english: 'outside, to a strange man.'
'Outside' implies that there is an 'inside' one,
phrases.notes: The 'inside' wife is the one who is a close relative of the יבם, the ערוה.

phrases.english: and the Merciful One says: 'shall not be.'
phrases.notes: So the outside co-wife may not marry a stranger. She is still bound to the brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by giving the Torah source behind בית שמאי's position in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'החוצה' we learn that even when there is an 'inside' wife (the ערוה), the 'outside' co-wife is still bound to יבום.

steps.title: בית הלל use the פסוק for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that בית הלל do not learn בית שמאי's lesson from this פסוק because they need it for רב's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? They need that פסוק for the teaching that רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assumes the question 'How do בית הלל deal with this פסוק?' and answers that they need it for another lesson. It is setting up the next step, which quotes that lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק is already being used to teach a different law, it is not free to teach בית שמאי's derivation. That way בית הלל can disagree without ignoring the פסוק. The details of the other lesson come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it, meaning the פסוק is needed for another teaching
For the teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel?

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב.
phrases.english: They need it for that which Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends בית הלל against the derivation of בית שמאי given in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק says 'החוצה,' it seems everyone must accept that the outside co-wife needs יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל use the פסוק for רב's law about קידושין of a יבמה, so it does not teach בית שמאי's point.

steps.title: רב's law: קידושין by an outsider do not take effect on a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches from the same פסוק that if a stranger tries to betroth a widow who is waiting for יבום, the קידושין do not take effect at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: How do we know that קידושין do not take effect on a יבמה? The פסוק says, 'The wife of the dead man shall not be outside, to a stranger,' meaning a stranger cannot have any marriage with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב's teaching, which explains what בית הלל learn from the פסוק instead of בית שמאי's lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'לא תהיה' as 'there shall be no הויה (marriage),' not merely 'she should not marry.' That makes a stranger's קידושין completely invalid while she is waiting for יבום or חליצה. Because the פסוק teaches this, בית הלל do not use it as proof that the צרה of an ערוה needs יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The betrothal does not take effect
A widow waiting for יבום or חליצה
Becoming married, a marriage bond
A stranger, someone other than the יבם

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי read 'החוצה' to show that the outside co-wife needs יבום. בית הלל use the same פסוק for רב's law that a stranger's קידושין do not take effect on a יבמה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying it is only forbidden for a stranger to marry her. He is saying the קידושין simply do not happen at all.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that betrothal does not take effect on a yevama?
phrases.notes: He means betrothal by someone other than the יבם, before she has done חליצה.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'The wife of the dead man shall not be'
'outside, to a strange man.'
There shall not be in her any becoming married to a stranger.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין קִידּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בִּיבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching that the previous step said בית הלל need the פסוק for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין by a stranger do not take effect on a יבמה, learned from 'לא תהיה... לאיש זר.'

steps.title: בית שמאי explain how they read the word ״חוּצָה״
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the פסוק says ״חוּצָה״, not ״לַחוּץ״, so it describes the woman herself as an 'outside' woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do בית שמאי respond? Does the פסוק say 'to the outside'? It says 'outside.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's reply to בית הלל's reading of the פסוק. בית שמאי say the exact wording points to their own lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל used the פסוק for רב's rule about marrying 'to the outside,' meaning to a stranger. בית שמאי reply that the word is not ״לַחוּץ״ ('to the outside') but ״חוּצָה״. For them it describes the woman as 'the outside one,' the co-wife who still needs יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Outside'. The word in the פסוק that both schools are reading
'To the outside'. The wording that would clearly mean marrying an outsider
'Is it written…?' A way of pointing out that the פסוק does not actually say that

phrases.english: And בית שמאי [how do they answer]?
Is it written 'to the outside'?
'Outside' is what is written!
phrases.notes: So the word describes the woman herself, the 'outside' co-wife, and not where she is going.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's defense of their reading against בית הלל's use of the פסוק for רב's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might mean 'to the outside,' that is, marrying a stranger.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית שמאי, ״חוּצָה״ describes the woman as an outsider, the co-wife.

steps.title: בית הלל say ״חוּצָה״ means the same as ״לַחוּץ״
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that ״חוּצָה״ is treated as if it said ״לַחוּץ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? Since it is written 'outside,' it is as if it were written 'to the outside.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל reply that the different spelling does not change the meaning. The proof for this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold that a ה at the end of a word works like a ל at the start, so both mean 'to.' That means ״חוּצָה״ means 'to the outside,' and the פסוק is about marrying a stranger, which supports רב's rule. The next step brings a ברייתא to back this up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since it is written'
'It is as if it were written'

phrases.english: And בית הלל [how do they answer]?
Since it is written 'outside,'
it is as if it were written 'to the outside.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's point about the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסוק says ״חוּצָה״, it cannot mean 'to the outside.'
steps.terutzMaskana: A ה at the end means the same as a ל at the beginning, so ״חוּצָה״ means 'to the outside.'

steps.title: A ברייתא proves that a ה at the end means 'to'
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה teaches that a word that needs a ל at its start can get a ה at its end instead, and the school of רבי ישמעאל gives examples.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי נחמיה says, any word that needs a ל at its beginning, the פסוק can put a ה at its end instead. And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught examples: אֵלִים becomes אֵלִימָה, מַחֲנַיִם becomes מַחֲנָיְמָה, מִצְרַיִם becomes מִצְרַיְמָה, and also דִּבְלָתָיְמָה, יְרוּשָׁלַיְמָה, מִדְבָּרָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support בית הלל's claim that ״חוּצָה״ means 'to the outside.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה gives the general rule that a ה at the end of a word means 'to,' just like a ל at the start. The school of רבי ישמעאל lists place names from תנ״ך that work this way, such as מִצְרַיְמָה meaning 'to מצרים.' So ״חוּצָה״ fits the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As it is taught' in a ברייתא. This brings a supporting source
A word
The פסוק put a ה at its end
A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Nechemya says:
Any word that needs a ל at its beginning,
the verse put a ה at its end instead.
phrases.notes: A ל at the start of a word means 'to,' and a ה at the end means the same thing.

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For example, 'Elim' becomes 'Elima' (to Elim),
'Machanayim' becomes 'Machanayma' (to Machanayim),
'Mitzrayim' becomes 'Mitzrayma' (to Egypt),
'Divlatayma' (to Divlatayim), 'Yerushalayma' (to Jerusalem), 'midbara' (to the wilderness).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for בית הלל's claim that ״חוּצָה״ equals ״לַחוּץ״.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's reading of ״חוּצָה״ as 'to the outside'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי נחמיה and the examples from the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: Where do בית שמאי learn רב's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where בית שמאי learn רב's rule, since they use ״חוּצָה״ for something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי, where do they learn the rule that רב יהודה said in the name of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to set up the next step. If בית שמאי use ״חוּצָה״ for the co-wife, where do they get רב's rule from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that if a stranger betroths a woman waiting for יבום, the קידושין do not take effect. בית הלל learned this from ״חוּצָה״. Since בית שמאי use that word for a different lesson, the גמרא wants to know their source for רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do they know it?' A request for a source

phrases.english: And בית שמאי,
that [rule] which רב יהודה said in the name of רב,
phrases.notes: This is the rule from Step 5: a stranger's betrothal of a woman waiting for יבום does not take effect.

phrases.english: from where do they learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that ״חוּצָה״ has been given to בית שמאי for another lesson, the גמרא asks for their source for רב's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: בית שמאי's source for רב's rule

steps.title: בית שמאי learn it from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn רב's rule from the words ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from 'to a stranger.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי get רב's rule from a different phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the dead brother's wife should not be ״לְאִישׁ זָר״, 'to a stranger.' בית שמאי learn from this that a stranger's קידושין do not work. That leaves ״חוּצָה״ free for their own lesson about the co-wife.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To a stranger', a man who is not one of the brothers
'It comes out from' or 'it is learned from'

phrases.english: It is learned from 'to a stranger.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי learn רב's rule from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״.

steps.title: Then בית הלל should also learn it from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ teaches רב's rule, בית הלל should learn it from there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל too, let them learn it from 'to a stranger'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ is enough to teach רב's rule, then בית הלל don't need ״חוּצָה״ for it either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said בית הלל could not use ״חוּצָה״ for בית שמאי's lesson because they needed it for רב's rule. But if ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ already teaches רב's rule, that reason falls away. So ״חוּצָה״ should seem free for בית הלל as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let them learn it from…' A suggestion that pushes back on the argument
'Also' or 'too'

phrases.english: And בית הלל too,
let them learn it from 'to a stranger'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל נָמֵי, תִּיפּוֹק לְהוּ מִ״לְּאִישׁ זָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns Step 10's answer into a challenge against Step 4's explanation of בית הלל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 4 that בית הלל need ״חוּצָה״ for רב's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ already teaches רב's rule, then ״חוּצָה״ is not needed for it, and בית הלל should be free to learn בית שמאי's lesson from it.

steps.title: Yes, and ״חוּצָה״ teaches that an ארוסה needs יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that בית הלל learn רב's rule from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״, and says they use ״חוּצָה״ to include an ארוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. So why do I need 'outside'? To include a woman who was only betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and gives בית הלל a new use for ״חוּצָה״. It teaches that even a woman who was only betrothed to the brother who died falls to יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא changes its explanation of בית הלל. They also learn רב's rule from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״. They use ״חוּצָה״ to include an ארוסה: she was never brought into her husband's home and is still 'outside,' yet she still needs יבום. Since the word is used for this, it is not free for בית שמאי's lesson about the co-wife.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Yes, that is indeed so.' Agreeing with the challenge
'Why do I need it?'
'To include' something more under the law
A woman who is betrothed but not yet fully married

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי use ״חוּצָה״ for the co-wife ('the outside woman'). בית הלל use it to include an ארוסה. Both schools learn רב's rule, that a stranger's קידושין don't work, from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not taking back רב's rule. It only changes the source בית הלל use for it, from ״חוּצָה״ to ״לְאִישׁ זָר״, and gives ״חוּצָה״ a new job.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so.
So why do I need 'outside'?
To include the betrothed woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts Step 11's challenge and gives a new reason why בית הלל do not use ״חוּצָה״ the way בית שמאי do.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the challenge and giving the word a new use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל need ״חוּצָה״ for רב's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל learn רב's rule from ״לְאִישׁ זָר״ and use ״חוּצָה״ to include an ארוסה in יבום.

steps.title: Each side and the extra letter ה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn that an ארוסה is included from the extra ה in ״הַחוּצָה״. בית הלל do not learn anything from the difference between ״חוּצָה״ and ״הַחוּצָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side (בית שמאי) learns it from the change from ״חוּצָה״ to ״הַחוּצָה״. And the other side (בית הלל) does not find any meaning in the change from ״חוּצָה״ to ״הַחוּצָה״.
steps.whatsHappening: In step 12, בית הלל used ״חוּצָה״ to include an ארוסה. Now the גמרא explains where בית שמאי learn the same idea, and why בית הלל do not learn it that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי already used the word ״חוּצָה״ for something else, so they need another source for the ארוסה. They find it in the extra letter ה: the פסוק could have said ״חוּצָה״ but said ״הַחוּצָה״. בית הלל hold that this small spelling difference is not enough to learn a הלכה from.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other side of the argument)
'Outside' / 'the outside one': the same word, written with and without an extra ה at the start
It does not mean anything to them; they do not learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that an ארוסה is included. They only disagree about which part of the פסוק teaches it.

phrases.english: And the other one: from "ḥutza" to "haḥutza".
phrases.notes: "The other one" here is בית שמאי. They learn the ארוסה from the extra ה the פסוק adds.

phrases.english: And the other one: "ḥutza" versus "haḥutza"
phrases.notes: Now "the other one" means בית הלל.

phrases.english: does not mean anything to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the exchange from step 12. It shows where בית שמאי get the ארוסה from, and why בית הלל cannot use that source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: There is an unspoken question: if בית שמאי use ״חוּצָה״ for something else, where do they learn that an ארוסה is included? And why don't בית הלל learn it from the extra ה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי learn it from the extra ה in ״הַחוּצָה״. בית הלל do not learn anything from that spelling difference.

steps.title: רבא: one prohibition cannot fall on another
steps.stepSummary: רבא says בית שמאי's real reason is the rule אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר. It is not a פסוק at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the reason of בית שמאי is that a prohibition does not take hold where another prohibition already exists.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a brand-new explanation for בית שמאי's view that צרות are permitted. Everything until now was based on reading the פסוק; רבא bases it on a general rule instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman was already forbidden to the living brother as אשת אח while his brother was alive. So the second prohibition, אחות אשה, cannot take hold on her. Since the ערוה prohibition never took hold, there is no real ערוה here to exempt her צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their reason
A prohibition does not take hold where another prohibition already exists
A prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves בית שמאי's opinion from a reading of the פסוק to a general rule found throughout ש״ס. The rest of this section tests whether that rule really works.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The reason of Beit Shammai
is that a prohibition does not take hold on a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the reading of the פסוק behind and offers a different reason for בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי permit the צרה because the ערוה prohibition (אחות אשה) cannot take hold on top of the earlier prohibition of אשת אח.

steps.title: What if the living brother married first?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule works when the dead brother married first. But if the living brother married first, the אחות אשה prohibition came first.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well where the dead brother married first and then the living brother married. Then the prohibition of a wife's sister cannot come and take hold on the prohibition of a brother's wife. But if the living brother married first and then the dead brother married, the prohibition of a wife's sister came first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא by flipping the order of the two marriages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the dead brother married first. Then אשת אח came first, and אחות אשה cannot take hold on top of it, so רבא's rule works. But suppose the living brother married her sister first. Then אחות אשה is the earlier prohibition. Now רבא's reason seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (said just before showing where it does not work)
A wife's sister (a forbidden relative)
A brother's wife (a forbidden relative)
Comes first

steps.confusionAlert: "Dead" and "living" are just names for the two brothers. They tell you which brother later died and which one is the יבם. In both cases, both brothers were alive when they got married.

phrases.english: It works well where the dead one married,
phrases.notes: "The dead one" means the brother who later died. He married one sister first.

phrases.english: and afterward the living one married —
the prohibition of a wife's sister does not come
and take hold on the prohibition of a brother's wife.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נָשָׂא חַי וְאַחַר כָּךְ נָשָׂא מֵת,
phrases.english: But where the living one married and afterward the dead one married,
the wife's sister prohibition comes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's rule from step 14 against a case where the order of the marriages is reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that בית שמאי rely on אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אחות אשה came first, it is the earlier prohibition. So the woman should be a real ערוה and should exempt her צרה, and רבא's reason no longer explains בית שמאי.

steps.title: Then she is an ערוה with no מצוה at all
steps.stepSummary: In the reversed case, the אשת אח prohibition never takes hold. So no מצוה of יבום applies to her, and her צרה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the prohibition of a brother's wife cannot come and take hold on the prohibition of a wife's sister, she becomes the צרה of an ערוה where there is no מצוה, and she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by running the same rule in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now אחות אשה came first, so the later prohibition, אשת אח, cannot take hold. That means the woman never has the status of a brother's wife for the יבם, so there is no מצוה of יבום for her at all. Her צרה is then the צרה of an ערוה in a case with no מצוה, and that צרה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
The co-wife of a woman who is a forbidden relative
In a case where there is no מצוה (of יבום)
She is permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The rule אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר works in both orders. Whichever prohibition comes second does not take hold, and either way the צרה ends up permitted according to בית שמאי.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אָתֵי אִיסּוּר אֵשֶׁת אָח
phrases.english: Since the prohibition of a brother's wife does not come
and take hold on the prohibition of a wife's sister,
she becomes the co-wife of a forbidden relative
phrases.notes: "She" here is the other wife, the צרה of the sister.

phrases.english: where there is no מצוה, and she is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אָתֵי אִיסּוּר אֵשֶׁת אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 and keeps רבא's rule standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the same rule in the other direction: the later prohibition (אשת אח) cannot take hold, so the case is outside the מצוה of יבום.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אחות אשה came first, the woman is a real ערוה inside the יבום situation, so her צרה should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: אשת אח never takes hold on her, so there is no מצוה of יבום with her. Her צרה is the צרה of an ערוה where there is no מצוה, and she is permitted.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say the חליצה ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that בית שמאי disqualify צרות who did חליצה, and asks why it needs saying, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If they did חליצה, בית שמאי disqualify them, etc. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks why it needs to be stated at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that the צרות really are obligated in יבום, so their חליצה is real and they become a חלוצה, who may not marry a כהן. And בית הלל hold the צרות are not connected to the יבם at all, so their חליצה means nothing. Both results follow from the basic מחלוקת, so the line seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: They performed חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Disqualify, meaning she may not marry a כהן
It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: If they performed חליצה, בית שמאי disqualify, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. 'Disqualify' means she can no longer marry a כהן, because she is now a חלוצה.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of רבא's reason and goes back to the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line about צרות who did חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling follows automatically from each side's basic view, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The line rejects רבי יוחנן בן נורי's proposal
steps.stepSummary: The line comes to reject רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who wanted צרות to do חליצה rather than יבום. The משנה teaches that בית הלל still treat them as fully fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to reject the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who said: Come, let us make a rule for the צרות that they should do חליצה and not יבום. The משנה teaches us that בית הלל declare them fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line is needed to teach us something about בית הלל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי wanted a rule that צרות always do חליצה. If that rule had been accepted, their חליצה would count for something, and they would be unfit for a כהן even according to בית הלל. The משנה tells us that בית הלל declare them fit, which shows that this proposal was not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, meaning this comes to reject another view
A תנא who proposed a new rule for the צרות
Let us make a rule, a rabbinic enactment
It teaches us, the new point being made
Declare fit, meaning allowed to marry a כהן

phrases.english: To exclude the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי,
who said: Come and let us make a rule for the צרות
that they should do חליצה and not do יבום.
It teaches us
that בית הלל declare them fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the line has a hidden novelty: it rejects another opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule was accepted, which would make the צרות unfit even according to בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: No such rule was accepted. According to בית הלל, the צרות stay fit for a כהן even after חליצה.
steps.confusionAlert: The question and answer are not mainly about בית שמאי. The real point of the line is that בית הלל declare these צרות fit.

steps.title: Why does the משנה also need the יבום ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line that if the צרות did יבום, בית הלל disqualify them, and asks why this is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If they did יבום, בית הלל disqualify them, etc. Why do I need this too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and again asks why it is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that בית הלל forbid the צרה to the יבם. So if she went ahead with יבום, it was a forbidden relationship, and of course she is now unfit for a כהן. This seems to follow from what was already taught.

keyTerms.meaning: They did יבום, meaning they married the brother-in-law
Why do I need this as well?

phrases.english: If they did יבום, בית הלל disqualify, etc.
Why do I need this as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same kind of question as step 17, now aimed at the משנה's next line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line about צרות who did יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling already follows from what was taught, so it looks repetitive.

steps.title: Said only to match the חליצה line
steps.stepSummary: Because the משנה taught the case of חליצה, it also taught the case of יבום, even though that was not strictly needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it taught 'they did חליצה,' it also taught 'they did יבום.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the line adds nothing new. It is there only so the משנה's wording stays parallel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a style answer, not a new law. The משנה wanted to present both cases side by side, so it included the יבום case along with the חליצה case.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it taught, meaning it was said along with the other case

steps.whatToRemember: The חליצה line teaches that רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule was not accepted, so בית הלל keep those צרות fit. The יבום line is there only to match it.

phrases.english: Since it taught 'they did חליצה,'
it also taught 'they did יבום.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Style parallel (אגב), with no new legal point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבום line must be teaching some new law.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches nothing new. It just matches the חליצה line.

steps.title: A משנה from מגילה about the days to read the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת מגילה: the מגילה may be read on the 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th or 15th, no earlier and no later.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: The מגילה is read on the 11th, the 12th, the 13th, the 14th, or the 15th, not earlier and not later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת to set up a new discussion. The next steps will build on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה lets different places read the מגילה on different days. The גמרא quotes it here as a base text, and the discussion it opens will follow in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, meaning in a משנה from another מסכת
מגילת אסתר, read on פורים
Not earlier and not later

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' is the opening משנה of מסכת מגילה.

phrases.english: The מגילה is read on the eleventh,
and on the twelfth, and on the thirteenth,
and on the fourteenth, and on the fifteenth,
not earlier and not later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the explanation of the משנה's wording ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מגילה may be read on any of the days from the 11th to the 15th of אדר, and on no other days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the starting point for the גמרא's next discussion, so keep its five days in mind.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks whether different reading days split the nation into groups
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ challenges the משנה of מגילה: having different reading days should break the rule of לא תתגודדו, which means 'do not become separate groups.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: Shouldn't we apply here the פסוק 'You shall not cut yourselves', meaning 'do not become many separate groups'?
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ challenges the משנה we just saw, which lets different places read the מגילה on different days. He says this seems to split the Jewish people into groups that act differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תתגודדו sounds like אגודות, 'groups.' So the פסוק is read as a warning against Jews in one area acting in clashing ways. Many reading days look like exactly that kind of split.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not cut yourselves' (דברים 14:1); also read as 'do not form separate groups'
Many separate groups or factions
'Should I read here', meaning: doesn't this פסוק apply to our case?

steps.whyThisMatters: This question about factions sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows, including the difference between a custom and a binding rule.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Should I apply here 'You shall not cut yourselves',
phrases.notes: דברים 14:1. 'Here' means the many different מגילה reading days from the last step.

phrases.english: meaning: do not become many separate groups?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the מגילה משנה quoted in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה allowing the מגילה to be read on different days in different places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different days for the same מצוה split the people into groups, which לא תתגודדו forbids.

steps.title: The verse seems to be about cutting for the dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא steps aside to ask how the factions rule can come from this פסוק, since it is needed for its plain meaning: not cutting yourself over a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: This 'You shall not cut yourselves' is needed for its own meaning, as the Torah says: do not make a wound on yourselves over a dead person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main question to ask a side question: how do we know this פסוק is about groups at all? Its plain meaning is about mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is fully used up by its plain meaning cannot easily teach a second lesson. So the גמרא asks for a reason to find the 'factions' teaching in it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for its own plain meaning
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
A wound or cut on the body

phrases.english: This 'You shall not cut yourselves'
is needed for its own matter,
as the Merciful One said:
do not make a wound over a dead person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the source that רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ used in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading לא תתגודדו as a rule against factions.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is needed for its plain meaning about cutting for the dead, so where is the extra lesson?

steps.title: The longer word form shows an extra lesson
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have used the shorter form תגודדו. The longer form תתגודדו hints at the extra lesson about groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should say 'לא תגודדו.' Why does it say 'תתגודדו'? Learn from this that it also comes for this lesson.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question: the word's form is longer than needed. That extra piece of the word teaches the rule about groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For cutting alone, the simpler form תגודדו would do. The added letters in תתגודדו are treated as extra, and extra wording teaches something new: not to split into groups.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let the פסוק say', meaning the Torah could have written it differently
'Learn from it', meaning we can conclude from this
It comes for this purpose

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say 'lo tegodedu.'
What is 'titgodedu'?
phrases.notes: Both forms mean 'cut yourselves'; the point is that the Torah chose the longer one.

phrases.english: Learn from it that it comes for this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by pointing to the unusual word form.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק teaches an additional lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only covers cutting for the dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: The longer form also teaches not to form separate groups.

steps.title: Maybe the whole verse is only about groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the entire פסוק is about groups and not about cutting for the dead at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the whole פסוק comes only for this lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges from the other side. If the word hints at groups, maybe that is all it means, and there is no ban on cutting for the dead here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer proved the 'groups' lesson. Now the worry is that it went too far and pushed out the plain meaning entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say', introducing another possible reading
All of it, the whole thing

phrases.english: But say that all of it
comes for this!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק teaches both lessons.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word form points to groups, maybe the whole פסוק is only about groups.

steps.title: The verse teaches both lessons
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק were only about cutting, it could have said תגודו. The form it uses teaches two things: no cutting for the dead and no splitting into groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should say 'לא תגודו.' Why does it say 'לא תתגודדו'? Learn from it two things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to yet another, even shorter way the Torah could have written the word. The full form we have shows the פסוק holds both lessons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning about cutting is not pushed aside; the extra form adds the lesson about groups on top. This ends the side discussion: the פסוק teaches both rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: לא תתגודדו teaches two things: do not cut yourselves over the dead, and do not split into separate groups.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say 'lo tagodu.'
What is 'lo titgodedu'?
Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 and closes the side discussion that began in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison with another possible word form shows both meanings are kept.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק might be only about groups.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches both the ban on cutting and the ban on factions.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן points to different local customs on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: Back to the main question: רבי יוחנן answers that we already learned places may have different customs about working on ערב פסח, so differences between places are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Have you not learned until now: in a place where people were used to working on ערב פסח until midday, they work; in a place where people were used not to work, they do not work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's main question. רבי יוחנן answers that a משנה already allows different places to act differently about work on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If different practices in different towns were forbidden factions, that משנה would not allow them. So, he argues, the different מגילה days should not be a problem either.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Have you not learned until now?', meaning you already know this
A place where the people had a custom
The day before פסח
Midday

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַד כָּאן לֹא שָׁנִיתָ
phrases.english: He said to him: Have you not learned until now:
phrases.notes: Here רבי יוחנן is the one speaking, answering רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.

phrases.english: a place where they were used to doing work
on the day before Pesach until midday, they work;

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת — אֵין עוֹשִׂין!
phrases.english: a place where they were used not to work, they do not work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main question of step 22 after the side discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a parallel case where different local practices are allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Different practices in different places break לא תתגודדו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different places may have different practices, as with work on ערב פסח.

steps.title: ריש לקיש rejects the proof: פורים is a rule, not a custom
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ answers that the פורים dates are a binding rule set by the חכמים, while work on ערב פסח is only a custom. A custom proves nothing about a rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am telling you about a prohibition, as רב שמן בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'To establish these days of פורים in their times' teaches that the חכמים set many times for them. And you tell me about a custom?!
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ pushes back on רבי יוחנן's proof. He says the ערב פסח case is only a custom, while the פורים days are a set rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different customs in different towns may be fine. But when the חכמים fix binding dates and people must follow different ones, the split is stronger and more like a real faction. He even quotes רבי יוחנן's own teaching to show the Purim dates are fixed by the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition, a binding rule
A custom, a local practice
In their times (אסתר 9:31)
They set up, they instituted

steps.confusionAlert: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ quotes a teaching of רבי יוחנן himself, said through רב שמן בר אבא, to answer רבי יוחנן. The person being quoted is not on רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's side of the argument; he is using his partner's own words.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between a custom and a binding rule is the key to whether differing practices count as forbidden factions.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אָמֵינָא לָךְ אֲנָא אִיסּוּרָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: I am telling you about a prohibition,
phrases.notes: He means the Purim reading days are a binding rule, not just a local habit.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rav Shemen bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
'To establish these days of Purim in their times':
phrases.notes: אסתר 9:31

phrases.english: the Sages set up many times for them,
and you tell me about a custom?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from ערב פסח given in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the Purim days and the ערב פסח custom.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ערב פסח case is only a custom, while the Purim days are a binding rule set by the חכמים, so the cases are not the same.

steps.title: Work on ערב פסח is also a real prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן pushes back: the ערב פסח case is not just a custom. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether work that night is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, is it not a prohibition? But we learned in a משנה: (At night) בית שמאי forbid work and בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's answer that ערב פסח is only a custom. He quotes a משנה showing it is a real argument about what is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ had said that custom proves nothing about a rule. רבי יוחנן shows that on ערב פסח there is a real איסור dispute: בית שמאי forbid and בית הלל permit. People follow different rulings, so there is a split about a real rule after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition; something forbidden by הלכה, not just a custom
But didn't we learn in a משנה? Opens a challenge from a משנה
The students of שמאי, the school that is usually stricter
The students of הלל, whose rulings we usually follow

phrases.english: And there, is it not a prohibition?
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of working on ערב פסח from the step before.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
(At night) בית שמאי forbid work,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. It means the night that starts ערב פסח.

phrases.english: and בית הלל permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's claim in Step 28 that the ערב פסח case is only a custom.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's distinction between a binding rule (Purim) and a custom (ערב פסח)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows a real איסור dispute about work that night. People follow different rulings, so differences about a real rule already exist.

steps.title: Not working does not look like a separate group
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ answers: on ערב פסח, someone who sees a person not working just thinks he has no work to do, so no one sees two groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, someone who sees him says: he simply has no work to do.
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ defends his view with a new reason. Even if the ערב פסח case is a real dispute, it does not look like people are splitting into groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem of לא תתגודדו is about splits people can see. A person resting can be explained in an innocent way: he has no job today. פורים is different, because reading the מגילה on different days is clearly visible.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who sees; an onlooker
Work, labor
That he does not have

steps.confusionAlert: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ is not taking back his position here. He keeps it and just gives a new reason why the ערב פסח case does not prove anything.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ is answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: There, someone who sees says:
It is work that he does not have.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's challenge in Step 29 by changing the reason the ערב פסח case does not count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: visible split versus split that no one can see
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ערב פסח involves a real איסור dispute, it should prove that different practices are allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not working can be explained innocently, so it does not look like groups. Only visible differences break לא תתגודדו.

steps.title: The visible dispute about צרות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings a case that is a real איסור and is clearly visible: בית שמאי permit the צרות to the brothers and בית הלל forbid them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But בית שמאי permit the rival wives to the brothers, and בית הלל forbid them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ again with a new example. Here both a real rule and a visible difference exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a צרה may marry the brother is a serious איסור, and a marriage is something everyone sees. Even so, בית שמאי and בית הלל each followed their own view. That looks like exactly the kind of split רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! Opens a challenge from a known fact
Rival wives; the other wives of a man who died, here the ones the משנה discusses
Brothers; the dead husband's brothers who might do יבום
Permit / forbid

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the לא תתגודדו discussion back to the main topic of the perek, the צרות. It sets up the question of how בית שמאי and בית הלל could act differently in such a visible matter.

phrases.english: But בית שמאי permit
the rival wives to the brothers,
and בית הלל forbid them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מַתִּירִין הַצָּרוֹת לָאַחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's reason in Step 30 with a case that is both a real איסור and clearly visible.
steps.kashyaTarget: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's claim that different practice about a real rule, done openly, breaks לא תתגודדו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the צרות dispute, the איסור is real and a marriage is visible. Still, each school followed its own ruling, so open differences seem to be allowed.
